"7d626c28-b73d-53d4-a3bf-5c54b8c980e1" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "7d626c28-b73d-53d4-a3bf-5c54b8c980e1" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{16}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{4}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "7d626c28-b73d-53d4-a3bf-5c54b8c980e1" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "7d626c28-b73d-53d4-a3bf-5c54b8c980e1" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{25}\cdot 5=\frac{4}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

$$

$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "175ef2ae-4064-5df6-a17e-4f826d7df838" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "175ef2ae-4064-5df6-a17e-4f826d7df838" :question/answer-fields "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7" :question/id #uuid "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7"] [:db/add "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{4}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "cb147313-6321-57c2-9e41-a59bfa74b9a7" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/answer-fields \int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/answer-fields "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/id #uuid "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f"] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{25}\cdot 5=\frac{3}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$

"8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/id #uuid "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79"] [:db/add "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{2}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(2 x \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "041f7d22-d8a1-5d07-866f-37bc0cf86bac" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "041f7d22-d8a1-5d07-866f-37bc0cf86bac" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{4}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.

"4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/id #uuid "4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33"] [:db/add "4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{4 x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{4}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
16 x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{4 x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{5}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{25}\cdot \frac{5}{4}=\frac{3}{20}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{20}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{20}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{20}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{20}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{4 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/answer-fields "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/id #uuid "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344"] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

\int \frac{1}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
9 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{6}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/answer-fields $$
9 x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{4})^2\right).

$$

$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{25}\cdot 5=\frac{4}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "9fac851b-355b-5020-8f36-949a9a05aba7" :question/answer-fields "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "795d7acd-3ce5-58cf-a7d2-51050e733863" :question/answer-fields "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "6f3ddf0d-e8b9-51fc-8fad-aee93d041c89" :question/answer-fields "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/id #uuid "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f"] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{25}\cdot 5=\frac{3}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{2}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "8b3918f5-78fb-5fb5-9645-bfe0e6ea1b79" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{2}{3}$.

$$

$$

Substitute back:

$$

$$

$$

$$

"1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/id #uuid "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344"] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
9 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{6}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "1319d74d-edf9-57c5-a8c2-0e37322fa344" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\frac{1}{8}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{8}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

$$

$$

$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "22967702-d9fa-58b6-9c26-8a737978cc3c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "22967702-d9fa-58b6-9c26-8a737978cc3c" :question/answer-fields Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
9 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "6f03ed92-b144-5b29-a6dd-49ded5b48710" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "6f03ed92-b144-5b29-a6dd-49ded5b48710" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

$$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["175ef2ae-4064-5df6-a17e-4f826d7df838" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot 2=\frac{3}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["175ef2ae-4064-5df6-a17e-4f826d7df838" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["175ef2ae-4064-5df6-a17e-4f826d7df838" :question/answer-fields "aa8d3463-8288-5beb-86c5-2dfa9d9d11d3"] ["2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{25}\cdot 5=\frac{3}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["2071ef75-3ba7-54a9-bd04-476183fbd47f" :question/answer-fields "1189176a-452e-507e-8347-a750813f29e5"] ["4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{4 x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{4}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
16 x^{2} + 25=25\left(1+(\frac{4 x}{5})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{5}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{25}\cdot \frac{5}{4}=\frac{3}{20}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{20}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{20}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{20}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{20}\left(\arctan{\left(\frac{4 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["4ad7da9a-3950-5b45-a79c-01458ad54f33" :question/answer-fields "8a4be29e-c874-5841-a197-2fd01d1bb5ed"] Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
9 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

$$"] ["6f03ed92-b144-5b29-a6dd-49ded5b48710" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["6f03ed92-b144-5b29-a6dd-49ded5b48710" :question/answer-fields "778e166a-1354-5c5b-8c80-4ae4f460f50e"]
